pitchfork.title: Stick Around for Tea
pitchfork.dek: The irreverent duo of Leo Fincham and Rowan Please plies its brilliantly digitized indie-pop bricolage on an album with the ragtag splendor of a low-budget musical.
pitchfork.label: self-released

pitchfork.title: DJ-Kicks
pitchfork.dek: The UK selector throws caution—and genre—to the winds on an audacious 82-minute set that careens between ambient, drill’n’bass, post-punk, breakcore, and more.
pitchfork.label: !K7

pitchfork.title: Autosmile
pitchfork.dek: The Philly duo’s folk music radiates a special kind of energy. Their second album is tinged with psychedelia, a wicker wunderkammer of songs, spells, and secrets.
pitchfork.label: 4AD

pitchfork.title: A Mile South of Heaven
pitchfork.dek: Torn between Texas and Topanga but fully herself, the songwriter sounds at home in the outlaw country idiom on an intimate, searching new record produced by Shooter Jennings.
pitchfork.label: New West

pitchfork.title: Dja Dja
pitchfork.dek: Modeled after the literary concept of the hero’s journey, the Catalan composer’s latest album is her most ambitious yet: It’s weirder, wilder, and more dazzling than anything she’s done to date.
pitchfork.label: Marina Herlop

pitchfork.title: Live at Carnegie Hall
pitchfork.dek: With new songs that rank among his very best, the Geese frontman’s solo live album is an exquisite rendering of a had-to-be-there night and a work of real-time mythmaking.
pitchfork.label: Partisan / Play It Again Sam

nme.dek: Still in recovery from a life-shattering stroke, the Mercury Prize winner offers a deeply poignant, lyrically brilliant glimpse into his state pre-illness

nme.album: I Hate You Don’t Leave Me !
nme.dek: a layered look at love, loss and self-doubt
coming to terms with the messiness of growing up

nme.album: I Think I Spoke Too Soon
nme.dek: a glittering comedown on the dancefloor
a doom-ridden escape from the band of the decade
extending a hopeful hand to a generation on the edge
funk-pop maximalist gets her hands dirty
